AUTHOR: M. Sirigineedi
TITLE: Improving Fisheries Management through Deep learning based Automated fish counting
VENUE: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
REGION: Washington State, USA (fish ladder counting window)
SPECIES: salmonids at fish ladder, labelled adipose / no_adipose / partially obscured
DATA: Phase 1: 168 web-scraped tourist photos of fish passing fishway viewing windows (augmented to 504 images, 725 labels); Phase 2: frames from a fish-ladder counting-site video (Washington)
V_EV: no statement found (only generic mention of fog/low light visibility)
D_EV: no statement found (only generic 'Divide the data set up ... for testing and training purposes')
R_EV: Sec. VIII: 'the model developed using images from Phase 2 exhibited an accuracy of 70%' (single source, no external test)
C_EV: no statement found of the threshold actually used (only generic: 'It is standard custom to adopt a confidence threshold, often set at 0.5')
E_EV: Sec. VIII: 'the accuracy of the model constructed using photographs from Phase 1 was determined to be 50%' (detection mAP only)
NOTE: Inclusion borderline: Phase 1 data are web-scraped tourist photos (would be excluded); Phase 2 are fishway counting-window video frames (in-situ fishway) with reported mAP 70%. Paper closely mirrors a Roboflow tutorial; methods poorly reported. Conclusion claims 'average absolute error per image down to 0.5 fish' with no supporting method/results -> E1 coded 없음. Generic 0.5 confidence threshold not clearly the one used -> C1=NR. Data source/test provenance vague.
